pics.alt: Map of the western United States coloured by the 2002–2023 trend in groundwater storage, with the strongest losses in California's Central Valley
pics.caption: Groundwater storage trends across the western United States, 2002–2023, from GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite gravimetry, in centimetres of water equivalent per year. The deepest losses (dark red) lie beneath the southern Central Valley (San Joaquin and Tulare basins) of California, where drought-era pumping has drawn down aquifers.

pics.alt: U.S. Drought Monitor map for 16 August 2022 showing D0 to D4 drought categories across the United States
pics.caption: The U.S. Drought Monitor for 16 August 2022, blending many indicators into categories D0 (abnormally dry) to D4 (exceptional drought). S and L labels mark short-term and long-term impacts; exceptional drought covers parts of the Far West and the southern Plains.
